The DeepSeek Harness implementation checkout is at C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh\. The checkout location and current working directory are separate values and may differ; never infer the working directory from this path. Use pwd to determine the current working directory. Use this checkout only to inspect or extend DSH itself.

You are interacting with the user through the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI at http://127.0.0.1:3080. When the user refers to "this page", "this GUI", or "this app" without naming another target, they mean this GUI. The browser provides no implicit DOM, route, or screenshot context. The client-plugin HMR receiver is active, but client-plugin changes reload without a refresh only while `pnpm run dev:web` is also running from this same checkout to rebuild their bundles; verify that watcher before promising automatic updates. You are a coding agent powered by the deepseek-v4-flash model. Your working directory is E:\Desktop\Openvela.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]` markers; investigate failures before moving on. On Windows a killed process settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker; treat a bare exit 1 after an interruption as a termination, not a command failure.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use the web_search tool to discover current information on the web. It returns an optional answer plus a list of source URLs. Use the returned source snippets when available, and cite the relevant URLs as markdown links.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Use the ralph tool ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks for a Ralph loop or fresh-agent iterative execution. Each Ralph round starts a fresh child with no conversation seed and uses the shared workspace as durable memory. Completion and blockers are worker reports, not independent evaluation. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Use subagent in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When you successfully create or modify files, mention the primary outputs in your final response. tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

Use the workflow tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow or for large multi-agent orchestration: you write a JavaScript script (the tool description documents the exact format) that fans work out across many subagents with phases and structured results. For one or two delegations, prefer plain subagent calls.

Use the ralph tool ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks for a Ralph loop or fresh-agent iterative execution. Each Ralph round starts a fresh child with no conversation seed and uses the shared workspace as durable memory. Completion and blockers are worker reports, not independent evaluation. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Use subagent in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

Use subagent_fork in the background by default. Start independent delegations together in one assistant message and continue useful work while they run. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. When a background run settles, the runtime sends you a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message.

When you successfully create or modify files, mention the primary outputs in your final response. To make those and any other changed-file references clickable in Web, format them as Markdown inline code using the exact file-tool path, or a basename when unique among the files changed in that turn.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

1: # 面向听障群体的端侧静态手语手势翻译终端 — OpenVela 适配计划书
2: 
3: > 版本：v1.1　日期：2026-08-11　状态：实施中
4: >
5: > **进度快照（2026-08-12）**：Phase 0（环境准备）✅ 100%；Phase 1（BSP 移植）~85%——芯片层/板级层代码已搬入、构建注册完成、芯片驱动 7 处兼容性修复已到位、首次编译走通到 C 代码编译阶段；唯一阻塞为 HAL 中 mbedtls 子模块的网络下载。详见 `开发进度日志.md` 与 `移植调研报告_ESP32P4.md`。
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 一、项目概述
10: 
11: - **项目名称**：面向听障群体的端侧静态手语手势翻译终端
12: - **一句话定位**：基于 ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board 与 OpenVela 系统，摄像头采集静态手语手势，端侧 AI 识别为文字并语音播报，解决听障人士简易日常沟通障碍。
13: - **核心功能（5 项）**：
14:   1. 摄像头采集手部图像，识别 12 种静态手语手势（字母 / 数字）
15:   2. 板载屏幕实时渲染摄像头画面 + 显示翻译文字
16:   3. 识别成功后本地播放预合成语音（WAV，不做端侧 TTS）
17:   4. WiFi 上传识别记录，网页查看历史日志
18:   5. 触摸屏切换识别模式、调整置信度阈值
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1.5 方案调整记录（2026-08-11 修订）
23: 
24: 基于环境搭建与源码核实，对原方案做以下调整（答辩与申报材料同步修改）：
25: 
26: ### 事实修正（避免答辩被质疑）
27: | 原表述 | 修正后 |
28: |--------|--------|
29: | 板载 NPU 神经网络加速器 | 400MHz 双核 RISC-V + AI 指令扩展（AI instruction extensions，官方术语，非独立 NPU），CPU 端侧推理 |
30: | 调用板载 NPU 完成推理 | 用 TFLite Micro（OpenVela 官方教程）在 CPU 上跑 INT8 模型 |
31: | 原生支持 OpenVela 系统 | 需自行移植，可复用 Apache NuttX 上游 esp32p4 BSP |
32: | WiFi6 蓝牙模组 | 由板载 ESP32-C6 协处理器通过 SDIO（ESP-Hosted）提供 |
33: 
34: ### 功能与技术方案调整
35: 1. **摄像头预览降负载**：7 寸屏实时预览用低分辨率（320×240）+ 识别结果叠加，降低带宽与 CPU 占用，把算力留给推理。
36: 2. **WiFi 上传降级预案**：识别日志先本地持久化（Flash/SD）；WiFi 上传为"锦上添花"，若 ESP32-C6 驱动一时调不通，用 USB 导出 / PC 端模拟上传演示，不影响主流程与评分核心。
37: 3. **数据采集提前并行**：12 类手势需自行采集标注，此项提前到 BSP 移植同期在 PC 上进行（模型训练不依赖板子），避免末期赶工。
38: 4. **AI 方案统一**：确定使用 TFLite Micro + INT8 量化轻量 CNN，不依赖专用加速器；推理延迟目标 <300ms。
39: 5. **语音播报保持原案**：预合成 12 段 WAV + 识别提示音，I2S 输出，不使用端侧 TTS。
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 二、关键现状核实（截至 2026-08-11，基于你本地 `docs-dev` 文档 + 官方 GitHub 仓库实测）
44: 
45: ### 2.1 编译环境约束（重要）
46: 
47: OpenVela 官方快速入门文档明确：
48: 
49: > 仅适配 **Ubuntu 22.04**，**不支持在 Windows 下直接编译，不支持 WSL / Docker 容器**。
50: 
51: - 硬件要求：≥40 GB 硬盘、≥16 GB 内存。
52: - 结论：**必须准备一台 Ubuntu 22.04 环境**（建议原生安装或独立虚拟机；WSL/Docker 官方不保证可用）。
53: 
54: ### 2.2 板卡支持现状：ESP32-P4 尚未被 OpenVela 支持
55: 
56: - 官方文档列出的开发板案例（STM32 系列、ESP32-S3-EYE、ESP32-S3-BOX、FC7300F8M、TC4D9、黄山派等）中 **没有 ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board**。
57: - 官方源码实测：
58:   - `open-vela/nuttx`（dev 分支）`arch/risc-v/src/` 下仅有 `esp32c3 / esp32c6 / esp32h2`，**无 `esp32p4`**；
59:   - `open-vela/vendor_espressif`（dev 与 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支）`boards/` 下仅有 `esp32s3`，**无 P4 板级**。
60: - 结论：**“板卡原生支持 OpenVela”目前不成立**。ESP32-P4 需自行移植，或等待比赛官方在 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支补充 BSP。
61: 
62: ### 2.3 好消息：上游 NuttX 已有完整 P4 支持可复用
63: 
64: Apache NuttX 上游已包含：
65: - 芯片层：`arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4/`
66: - 板级层：`boards/risc-v/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev-board/`（含 common、esp32p4-pico-wifi-wareshare、esp32p4-tab5 等）
67: 
68: OpenVela 基于 NuttX，因此**可将上游芯片/板级代码移植到 OpenVela 的 vendor 结构**，大幅降低工作量。
69: 
70: ### 2.4 硬件规格修正（答辩防坑）
71: 
72: 需求书中有三处与芯片实际规格不符，建议修正措辞：
73: 1. **“内置 NPU 神经网络加速器”**：ESP32-P4 芯片官方规格中没有独立 NPU。其 AI 加速依赖 400 MHz 双核 RISC-V 的 AI 指令扩展（AI instruction extensions）与 HiFi4 DSP。对 12 类轻量 CNN 完全够用，但答辩时“调用板载 NPU”的说法需改为“CPU + 向量扩展推理”或核实 PDF 是否另有专用加速器。
74: 2. **“WiFi6 蓝牙模组”**：P4 芯片本身无无线；P4-Function-EV-Board 通过板载 **ESP32-C6 协处理器**提供 WiFi6 / BLE5。
75: 3. **“原生支持 OpenVela 系统”**：见 2.2，目前需自行移植。
76: 
77: > 以上三条建议在比赛申报材料中改为：“板卡生态与 OpenVela 同为乐鑫/开源路线，具备移植可行性，且上游 NuttX 已有 BSP 参考”。
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 三、总体架构
82: 
83: ```
84: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
85: │  应用层（本项目开发）                                          │
86: │  手语翻译应用 app_sign_translate                             │
87: │  ├─ 手势识别引擎（TFLite Micro / ESP-DL，INT8 模型）           │
88: │  ├─ LVGL UI（摄像头预览 + 识别文字 + 模式/阈值设置界面）        │
89: │  ├─ 语音播报（WAV 播放，I2S 输出）                             │
90: │  └─ 日志上报（HTTP + JSON → 云端网页）                        │
91: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
92: │  OpenVela 系统服务层（NuttX）                                 │
93: │  ├─ LVGL 图形栈 / VIDEO / AUDIO / NET（TCP-IP, WiFi）        │
94: │  ├─ 驱动：MIPI-DSI LCD、触摸、MIPI-CSI 摄像头、I2S/Codec      │
95: │  └─ 文件系统（LittleFS/ROMFS 存模型与 wav 片段）              │
96: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
97: │  BSP 层（本次主要移植对象）                                    │
98: │  ├─ arch：arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4（自 NuttX 上游移植）        │
99: │  ├─ board：vendor/espressif/boards/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev│
100: │  └─ 工具链：riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc + esptool                 │
101: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
102:          硬件：ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board（P4 + ESP32-C6）
103: ```
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## 四、适配方案总览
108: 
109: ### 方案 A：等待官方 BSP（低风险但被动）
110: - 比赛使用 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支，官方可能陆续补齐 ESP32-P4 BSP。
111: - 动作：开赛前先确认比赛资料 / 群公告是否提供 P4 固件与 BSP；若提供则直接在其上做应用。
112: 
113: ### 方案 B：从 NuttX 上游移植（主动，推荐）
114: - 移植范围：
115:   1. 芯片层：`nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4` → OpenVela 的 `nuttx` 对应目录（或 vendor 结构）；
116:   2. 板级层：`boards/risc-v/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev-board` → `vendor/espressif/boards/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev/`，按 OpenVela 的 `vendor` 目录规范改写（Kconfig、Make.defs、ld.script、`src/<vendor>_boot.c / _bringup.c / _appinit.c`）；
117:   3. 工具链：安装 RISC-V 交叉编译工具链，烧录用 esptool。
118: - 参照文档：`docs-dev/zh-cn/chip_porting/porting_guide.md`（新平台适配指南）、`Vendor.md`（vendor 目录规范）、`quickstart/development_board/ESP32-S3-EYE.md`（同类板移植范例，含完整 defconfig）。
119: 
120: **建议：方案 B 为主线，方案 A 随时保持同步**（比赛分支一旦更新 P4 BSP，优先切换）。
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 五、分阶段实施计划（每阶段含目标 / 关键工作 / 验收标准）
125: 
126: ### Phase 0：环境准备（0.5 周）
127: - 目标：可编译、可烧录的最小闭环。
128: - 工作：
129:   1. 安装 Ubuntu 22.04（或独立虚拟机），装 git / curl / cmake / python3 / build-essential / Git LFS；
130:   2. 安装 VS Code（≥1.99）与 openvela 插件：`vela.vs-aiot-ide-vela`、`vela.vela-preview`（可选命令行方式）；
131:   3. `repo init`（GitHub 或 Gitee，dev 分支）→ `repo sync -c -j8`；
132:   4. 安装 RISC-V 工具链（`riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc`）与 esptool。
133: - 验收：成功编译任一已有配置（如 goldfish-arm64 模拟器 / esp32s3 配置），模拟器可启动 `lvgldemo`。
134: - 注意事项：工作目录绝对路径**禁止含中文/空格**（当前 `E:\Desktop\Openvela` 有中文，仅作资料存放，源代码要放到无中文路径）。
135: 
136: ### Phase 1：BSP 移植，让 OpenVela 在 P4 板上跑起来（2~3 周，风险最高）
137: - 目标：板子启动到 NSH，串口可交互。
138: - 工作：
139:   1. 核对 OpenVela nuttx 是否已含 `arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4`；没有则从 Apache NuttX 移植（重点：`esp32p4_start.c`、`esp32p4_irq.c`、`esp32p4_lowputc.c`、`esp32p4_timer.c`、Kconfig、Make.defs）；
140:   2. 创建 `vendor/espressif/boards/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev/` 目录结构（configs/nsh、include/board.h、scripts/ld.script+Make.defs、src/boot/bringup/appinit、etc/rcS 等）；
141:   3. 编写最小 defconfig：串口 console、时钟、PSRAM、基础 FS；
142:   4. 编译 → 用 esptool 烧录 → NSH 验证 `ifconfig`/`ls`/GPIO 点灯。
143: - 验收：上电打印 OpenVela 启动日志，`nsh>` 可用，板载 LED 可控制。
144: - 里程碑 M1：**BSP 点亮**（本阶段为整个项目成败关键，预留最多缓冲时间）。
145: 
146: ### Phase 2：显示 + 触摸（1 周）
147: - 目标：7 寸 MIPI-DSI 屏亮起来，LVGL 出画面，触摸可点。
148: - 工作：
149:   1. 移植/启用 esp32p4 MIPI-DSI 与 LCD panel 驱动；
150:   2. 启用 `CONFIG_GRAPHICS_LVGL`、`CONFIG_LV_USE_NUTTX_LCD`、触摸驱动，参考 esp32s3 defconfig 里的 LVGL 配置段；
151:   3. 跑通 `lvgldemo` 或自制 UI。
152: - 验收：屏幕显示 LVGL 界面，触摸点击有响应。
153: 
154: ### Phase 3：摄像头采集（1 周）
155: - 目标：摄像头出图并送入预处理。
156: - 工作：
157:   1. 启用 esp32p4 MIPI-CSI 驱动与 VIDEO 框架（`CONFIG_VIDEO*`）；
158:   2. 适配板载摄像头 sensor 驱动（以板子实际 sensor 型号为准，如 GC2145 / OV2640 类）；
159:   3. 输出预览帧（送 LVGL，建议低分辨率 320×240 以降低负载）与预处理帧（裁剪、灰度、缩放 96×96/128×128）。
160: - 验收：屏幕实时显示摄像头画面（低分辨率预览）；可抓取一帧灰度图供后续推理。
161: 
162: ### Phase 4：音频播报（0.5 周）
163: - 目标：识别成功后播放预合成 WAV。
164: - 工作：启用 I2S + 音频 codec 驱动，用 OpenVela 音频框架或直接 I2S DMA 播放 WAV；预生成 12 个手势的语音片段。
165: - 验收：程序触发可听到对应语音。
166: 
167: ### Phase 5：网络上传（1 周）
168: - 目标：WiFi6 联网，HTTP 上传 JSON 日志，网页可查。
169: - 工作：
170:   1. 启用 ESP32-C6 协处理器无线（SDIO/SPI/UART 与 C6 通信，以 BSP 支持方式为准）+ WiFi 协议栈（参考 esp32s3 defconfig 的 `CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI*` / 网络段）；
171:   2. 用 `CONFIG_NETUTILS_HTTPD` 或自写 socket 实现 HTTP POST JSON；
172:   3. 云端搭简易 Web 服务（如本地 Python Flask / 免费云）存储与展示日志。
173: - 验收：板子上传后网页能看到识别记录。
174: - **降级预案**：若 C6 WiFi 驱动迟迟不通，识别日志先本地持久化（LittleFS/SD），演示时用 USB 导出或 PC 端模拟上传，不阻塞其他功能。
175: 
176: ### Phase 6：AI 识别（2 周，与 Phase 1 可并行）
177: - 目标：12 类手势 INT8 模型在端侧跑通。
178: - 工作：
179:   1. 采集/整理 12 类静态手势数据集（字母+数字），PC 端训练轻量 CNN（如 MobileNetV2-0.5 或自定义浅 CNN，目标 <300 KB）；
180:   2. INT8 量化（PTQ 优先，必要时 QAT），转 `.tflite`；
181:   3. `xxd -i` 转 C 数组（`alignas(16) const`，放 Flash），集成 TFLite Micro（参照 `docs-dev/zh-cn/edge_ai_dev/` 三篇文档：overview / integration / model_integration）；
182:   4. 默认 CPU + 向量扩展推理（TFLite Micro），不依赖专用 NPU；数据采集与模型训练在 PC 上提前并行开展。
183: - 验收：对测试集分类准确率 ≥90%，单次推理延迟 <300 ms。
184: 
185: ### Phase 7：应用集成与演示（1 周）
186: - 目标：5 大功能串成完整演示。
187: - 工作：
188:   1. 手语翻译应用 `app_sign_translate`：采集 → 推理 → LVGL 显示文字 → 语音播报 → 日志上传；
189:   2. 触摸切换模式（数字/字母）与置信度阈值设置；
190:   3. 稳定性测试（长时间运行不崩溃），按 `porting_guide` 的 xTS 精简集跑一遍 BSP 基础用例。
191: - 验收：完整演示视频 + 答辩材料。
192: 
193: **总工期建议：8~10 周（其中 BSP 移植留 3 周缓冲）。**
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## 六、关键目录结构规划
198: 
199: ```
200: openvela/
201: ├── nuttx/
202: │   └── arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4/          # 芯片层（自 NuttX 上游移植/核对）
203: ├── vendor/espressif/
204: │   ├── boards/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev/
205: │   │   ├── configs/nsh/defconfig         # 基础 NSH 配置
206: │   │   ├── configs/ai/defconfig          # 本项目完整配置（AI+LVGL+相机+音频+网络）
207: │   │   ├── include/board.h
208: │   │   ├── scripts/ld.script, Make.defs
209: │   │   └── src/ espressif_boot.c, _bringup.c, _appinit.c
210: │   └── prebuilt/ riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
211: └── apps/ (或 vendor 内)
212:     └── examples/sign_translate/          # 手语翻译应用
213:         ├── sign_translate_main.cxx
214:         ├── model_data.cc                 # INT8 模型数组
215:         ├── audio/ *.wav                  # 预合成语音片段
216:         └── CMakeLists.txt
217: ```
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## 七、风险与对策
222: 
223: | # | 风险 | 等级 | 对策 |
224: |---|------|------|------|
225: | 1 | OpenVela 无现成 P4 BSP，芯片层移植难 | 高 | 优先复用 NuttX 上游 esp32p4；提前确认比赛官方是否提供 BSP；Phase 1 预留最多时间 |
226: | 2 | 环境必须是 Ubuntu 22.04，Windows 用户不便 | 高 | 尽快搭 Ubuntu 22.04（原生/虚拟机）；不依赖 WSL/Docker |
227: | 3 | “NPU”实为 CPU 向量扩展，推理延迟不确定 | 中 | 12 类静态手势用轻量 CNN，400 MHz 双核足够；提前压测延迟，必要时缩小输入分辨率 |
228: | 4 | WiFi6 依赖 ESP32-C6 协处理器，驱动/协议栈适配复杂 | 中 | 先以“能联网上传”为目标（不苛求 6 代速率）；预留降级方案（USB/SD 卡导出日志） |
229: | 5 | 摄像头 sensor 驱动无现成支持 | 中 | 优先用 NuttX/ESP-IDF 已有支持的 sensor 型号，或先用官方 demo 库抓图 |
230: | 6 | 比赛分支代码变动 | 低 | 定期 `repo sync`，关注 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支更新 |
231: | 7 | 数据准备与标注耗时 | 中 | 提前开始采集 12 类手势数据；用数据增强扩大样本 |
232: 
233: ---
234: 
235: ## 八、待确认事项清单（评审会前请逐项确认）
236: 
237: 1. 比赛是否提供 ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board 的 OpenVela BSP / 固件？在哪个分支？
238: 2. PDF 硬件资料中板载摄像头 sensor 型号、屏幕分辨率/接口、音频 codec 型号、C6 与 P4 连接方式？（可把 PDF 关键页转成文字/图片发我，我帮你梳理驱动需求）
239: 3. 比赛对“云端日志”有无指定平台？是否允许自建本地服务演示？
240: 4. 手语手势定义：12 类具体是哪些字母/数字？有无标准数据集或必须自采？
241: 5. 答辩/评分侧重（BSP 移植深度 vs 应用完整度 vs AI 效果），决定时间分配。
242: 
243: ---
244: 
245: ## 九、工具链与 VS Code 问题解答
246: 
247: **需要 VS Code 参与吗？——建议使用，但不是硬性必须。**
248: 
249: - OpenVela 官方提供 **VS Code 插件**（`vela.vs-aiot-ide-vela` + `vela.vela-preview`），支持图形化“创建项目 → 配置 defconfig → 编译 → 模拟器运行 → 断点调试”全流程，还带图片/字体/资源预览，**调试功能必须依赖该插件（C++ 插件）**，对学生很友好。
250: - 不装插件也能开发：命令行 `./build.sh <defconfig路径> -j$(nproc)` 编译 + esptool 烧录 + GDB 调试。
251: - **硬性前提**：VS Code 与插件必须在 **Ubuntu 22.04** 上运行（Windows 版 VS Code 无法编译 OpenVela，官方不支持 WSL/Docker）。
252: - 结论：**在 Ubuntu 22.04 上安装 VS Code + openvela 插件**，作为主力开发 IDE；命令行作为备用。
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: ## 十、下一步建议动作（确认计划后执行）
257: 
258: 1. 确认第八节“待确认事项”，尤其是比赛是否提供 P4 BSP；
259: 2. 搭建 Ubuntu 22.04 环境 + VS Code + openvela 插件，跑通官方快速入门（模拟器）；
260: 3. 开始 Phase 1 BSP 移植调研（先核对 OpenVela nuttx 是否有 esp32p4，无则评估上游代码量）；
261: 4. 并行启动数据集收集与模型训练（Phase 6 前置）。

lines.text: # 面向听障群体的端侧静态手语手势翻译终端 — OpenVela 适配计划书
> **进度快照（2026-08-12）**：Phase 0（环境准备）✅ 100%；Phase 1（BSP 移植）~85%——芯片层/板级层代码已搬入、构建注册完成、芯片驱动 7 处兼容性修复已到位、首次编译走通到 C 代码编译阶段；唯一阻塞为 HAL 中 mbedtls 子模块的网络下载。详见 `开发进度日志.md` 与 `移植调研报告_ESP32P4.md`。
- **项目名称**：面向听障群体的端侧静态手语手势翻译终端
- **一句话定位**：基于 ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board 与 OpenVela 系统，摄像头采集静态手语手势，端侧 AI 识别为文字并语音播报，解决听障人士简易日常沟通障碍。
1. 摄像头采集手部图像，识别 12 种静态手语手势（字母 / 数字）
2. 板载屏幕实时渲染摄像头画面 + 显示翻译文字
3. 识别成功后本地播放预合成语音（WAV，不做端侧 TTS）
4. WiFi 上传识别记录，网页查看历史日志
5. 触摸屏切换识别模式、调整置信度阈值
基于环境搭建与源码核实，对原方案做以下调整（答辩与申报材料同步修改）：
### 事实修正（避免答辩被质疑）
| 板载 NPU 神经网络加速器 | 400MHz 双核 RISC-V + AI 指令扩展（AI instruction extensions，官方术语，非独立 NPU），CPU 端侧推理 |
| 调用板载 NPU 完成推理 | 用 TFLite Micro（OpenVela 官方教程）在 CPU 上跑 INT8 模型 |
| 原生支持 OpenVela 系统 | 需自行移植，可复用 Apache NuttX 上游 esp32p4 BSP |
| WiFi6 蓝牙模组 | 由板载 ESP32-C6 协处理器通过 SDIO（ESP-Hosted）提供 |
1. **摄像头预览降负载**：7 寸屏实时预览用低分辨率（320×240）+ 识别结果叠加，降低带宽与 CPU 占用，把算力留给推理。
2. **WiFi 上传降级预案**：识别日志先本地持久化（Flash/SD）；WiFi 上传为"锦上添花"，若 ESP32-C6 驱动一时调不通，用 USB 导出 / PC 端模拟上传演示，不影响主流程与评分核心。
3. **数据采集提前并行**：12 类手势需自行采集标注，此项提前到 BSP 移植同期在 PC 上进行（模型训练不依赖板子），避免末期赶工。
4. **AI 方案统一**：确定使用 TFLite Micro + INT8 量化轻量 CNN，不依赖专用加速器；推理延迟目标 <300ms。
5. **语音播报保持原案**：预合成 12 段 WAV + 识别提示音，I2S 输出，不使用端侧 TTS。
## 二、关键现状核实（截至 2026-08-11，基于你本地 `docs-dev` 文档 + 官方 GitHub 仓库实测）
OpenVela 官方快速入门文档明确：
> 仅适配 **Ubuntu 22.04**，**不支持在 Windows 下直接编译，不支持 WSL / Docker 容器**。
- 硬件要求：≥40 GB 硬盘、≥16 GB 内存。
- 结论：**必须准备一台 Ubuntu 22.04 环境**（建议原生安装或独立虚拟机；WSL/Docker 官方不保证可用）。
### 2.2 板卡支持现状：ESP32-P4 尚未被 OpenVela 支持
- 官方文档列出的开发板案例（STM32 系列、ESP32-S3-EYE、ESP32-S3-BOX、FC7300F8M、TC4D9、黄山派等）中 **没有 ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board**。
- `open-vela/nuttx`（dev 分支）`arch/risc-v/src/` 下仅有 `esp32c3 / esp32c6 / esp32h2`，**无 `esp32p4`**；
- `open-vela/vendor_espressif`（dev 与 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支）`boards/` 下仅有 `esp32s3`，**无 P4 板级**。
- 结论：**“板卡原生支持 OpenVela”目前不成立**。ESP32-P4 需自行移植，或等待比赛官方在 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支补充 BSP。
### 2.3 好消息：上游 NuttX 已有完整 P4 支持可复用
OpenVela 基于 NuttX，因此**可将上游芯片/板级代码移植到 OpenVela 的 vendor 结构**，大幅降低工作量。
### 2.4 硬件规格修正（答辩防坑）
需求书中有三处与芯片实际规格不符，建议修正措辞：
1. **“内置 NPU 神经网络加速器”**：ESP32-P4 芯片官方规格中没有独立 NPU。其 AI 加速依赖 400 MHz 双核 RISC-V 的 AI 指令扩展（AI instruction extensions）与 HiFi4 DSP。对 12 类轻量 CNN 完全够用，但答辩时“调用板载 NPU”的说法需改为“CPU + 向量扩展推理”或核实 PDF 是否另有专用加速器。
2. **“WiFi6 蓝牙模组”**：P4 芯片本身无无线；P4-Function-EV-Board 通过板载 **ESP32-C6 协处理器**提供 WiFi6 / BLE5。
3. **“原生支持 OpenVela 系统”**：见 2.2，目前需自行移植。
> 以上三条建议在比赛申报材料中改为：“板卡生态与 OpenVela 同为乐鑫/开源路线，具备移植可行性，且上游 NuttX 已有 BSP 参考”。
│  ├─ 手势识别引擎（TFLite Micro / ESP-DL，INT8 模型）           │
│  ├─ LVGL UI（摄像头预览 + 识别文字 + 模式/阈值设置界面）        │
│  ├─ 语音播报（WAV 播放，I2S 输出）                             │
│  └─ 日志上报（HTTP + JSON → 云端网页）                        │
│  ├─ LVGL 图形栈 / VIDEO / AUDIO / NET（TCP-IP, WiFi）        │
│  ├─ 驱动：MIPI-DSI LCD、触摸、MIPI-CSI 摄像头、I2S/Codec      │
│  └─ 文件系统（LittleFS/ROMFS 存模型与 wav 片段）              │
│  BSP 层（本次主要移植对象）                                    │
### 方案 A：等待官方 BSP（低风险但被动）
- 比赛使用 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支，官方可能陆续补齐 ESP32-P4 BSP。
- 动作：开赛前先确认比赛资料 / 群公告是否提供 P4 固件与 BSP；若提供则直接在其上做应用。
### 方案 B：从 NuttX 上游移植（主动，推荐）
1. 芯片层：`nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4` → OpenVela 的 `nuttx` 对应目录（或 vendor 结构）；

2. 板级层：`boards/risc-v/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev-board` → `vendor/espressif/boards/esp32p4/esp32p4-function-ev/`，按 OpenVela 的 `vendor` 目录规范改写（Kconfig、Make.defs、ld.script、`src/<vendor>_boot.c / _bringup.c / _appinit.c`）；
3. 工具链：安装 RISC-V 交叉编译工具链，烧录用 esptool。
- 参照文档：`docs-dev/zh-cn/chip_porting/porting_guide.md`（新平台适配指南）、`Vendor.md`（vendor 目录规范）、`quickstart/development_board/ESP32-S3-EYE.md`（同类板移植范例，含完整 defconfig）。
**建议：方案 B 为主线，方案 A 随时保持同步**（比赛分支一旦更新 P4 BSP，优先切换）。
## 五、分阶段实施计划（每阶段含目标 / 关键工作 / 验收标准）
- 目标：可编译、可烧录的最小闭环。
1. 安装 Ubuntu 22.04（或独立虚拟机），装 git / curl / cmake / python3 / build-essential / Git LFS；
2. 安装 VS Code（≥1.99）与 openvela 插件：`vela.vs-aiot-ide-vela`、`vela.vela-preview`（可选命令行方式）；
3. `repo init`（GitHub 或 Gitee，dev 分支）→ `repo sync -c -j8`；
4. 安装 RISC-V 工具链（`riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc`）与 esptool。
- 验收：成功编译任一已有配置（如 goldfish-arm64 模拟器 / esp32s3 配置），模拟器可启动 `lvgldemo`。
- 注意事项：工作目录绝对路径**禁止含中文/空格**（当前 `E:\Desktop\Openvela` 有中文，仅作资料存放，源代码要放到无中文路径）。
### Phase 1：BSP 移植，让 OpenVela 在 P4 板上跑起来（2~3 周，风险最高）
- 目标：板子启动到 NSH，串口可交互。
1. 核对 OpenVela nuttx 是否已含 `arch/risc-v/src/esp32p4`；没有则从 Apache NuttX 移植（重点：`esp32p4_start.c`、`esp32p4_irq.c`、`esp32p4_lowputc.c`、`esp32p4_timer.c`、Kconfig、Make.defs）；
3. 编写最小 defconfig：串口 console、时钟、PSRAM、基础 FS；
4. 编译 → 用 esptool 烧录 → NSH 验证 `ifconfig`/`ls`/GPIO 点灯。
- 验收：上电打印 OpenVela 启动日志，`nsh>` 可用，板载 LED 可控制。
- 里程碑 M1：**BSP 点亮**（本阶段为整个项目成败关键，预留最多缓冲时间）。
- 目标：7 寸 MIPI-DSI 屏亮起来，LVGL 出画面，触摸可点。
1. 移植/启用 esp32p4 MIPI-DSI 与 LCD panel 驱动；
2. 启用 `CONFIG_GRAPHICS_LVGL`、`CONFIG_LV_USE_NUTTX_LCD`、触摸驱动，参考 esp32s3 defconfig 里的 LVGL 配置段；
- 验收：屏幕显示 LVGL 界面，触摸点击有响应。
- 目标：摄像头出图并送入预处理。
1. 启用 esp32p4 MIPI-CSI 驱动与 VIDEO 框架（`CONFIG_VIDEO*`）；
2. 适配板载摄像头 sensor 驱动（以板子实际 sensor 型号为准，如 GC2145 / OV2640 类）；
3. 输出预览帧（送 LVGL，建议低分辨率 320×240 以降低负载）与预处理帧（裁剪、灰度、缩放 96×96/128×128）。
- 验收：屏幕实时显示摄像头画面（低分辨率预览）；可抓取一帧灰度图供后续推理。
- 目标：识别成功后播放预合成 WAV。
- 工作：启用 I2S + 音频 codec 驱动，用 OpenVela 音频框架或直接 I2S DMA 播放 WAV；预生成 12 个手势的语音片段。
- 验收：程序触发可听到对应语音。
- 目标：WiFi6 联网，HTTP 上传 JSON 日志，网页可查。
1. 启用 ESP32-C6 协处理器无线（SDIO/SPI/UART 与 C6 通信，以 BSP 支持方式为准）+ WiFi 协议栈（参考 esp32s3 defconfig 的 `CONFIG_WIRELESS_WAPI*` / 网络段）；
2. 用 `CONFIG_NETUTILS_HTTPD` 或自写 socket 实现 HTTP POST JSON；
3. 云端搭简易 Web 服务（如本地 Python Flask / 免费云）存储与展示日志。
- 验收：板子上传后网页能看到识别记录。
- **降级预案**：若 C6 WiFi 驱动迟迟不通，识别日志先本地持久化（LittleFS/SD），演示时用 USB 导出或 PC 端模拟上传，不阻塞其他功能。
### Phase 6：AI 识别（2 周，与 Phase 1 可并行）
- 目标：12 类手势 INT8 模型在端侧跑通。
1. 采集/整理 12 类静态手势数据集（字母+数字），PC 端训练轻量 CNN（如 MobileNetV2-0.5 或自定义浅 CNN，目标 <300 KB）；
2. INT8 量化（PTQ 优先，必要时 QAT），转 `.tflite`；
3. `xxd -i` 转 C 数组（`alignas(16) const`，放 Flash），集成 TFLite Micro（参照 `docs-dev/zh-cn/edge_ai_dev/` 三篇文档：overview / integration / model_integration）；
4. 默认 CPU + 向量扩展推理（TFLite Micro），不依赖专用 NPU；数据采集与模型训练在 PC 上提前并行开展。
- 验收：对测试集分类准确率 ≥90%，单次推理延迟 <300 ms。
### Phase 7：应用集成与演示（1 周）
- 目标：5 大功能串成完整演示。
1. 手语翻译应用 `app_sign_translate`：采集 → 推理 → LVGL 显示文字 → 语音播报 → 日志上传；
2. 触摸切换模式（数字/字母）与置信度阈值设置；
3. 稳定性测试（长时间运行不崩溃），按 `porting_guide` 的 xTS 精简集跑一遍 BSP 基础用例。
- 验收：完整演示视频 + 答辩材料。
**总工期建议：8~10 周（其中 BSP 移植留 3 周缓冲）。**

│   │   ├── configs/nsh/defconfig         # 基础 NSH 配置
│   │   ├── configs/ai/defconfig          # 本项目完整配置（AI+LVGL+相机+音频+网络）
| # | 风险 | 等级 | 对策 |
| 1 | OpenVela 无现成 P4 BSP，芯片层移植难 | 高 | 优先复用 NuttX 上游 esp32p4；提前确认比赛官方是否提供 BSP；Phase 1 预留最多时间 |
| 2 | 环境必须是 Ubuntu 22.04，Windows 用户不便 | 高 | 尽快搭 Ubuntu 22.04（原生/虚拟机）；不依赖 WSL/Docker |
| 3 | “NPU”实为 CPU 向量扩展，推理延迟不确定 | 中 | 12 类静态手势用轻量 CNN，400 MHz 双核足够；提前压测延迟，必要时缩小输入分辨率 |
| 4 | WiFi6 依赖 ESP32-C6 协处理器，驱动/协议栈适配复杂 | 中 | 先以“能联网上传”为目标（不苛求 6 代速率）；预留降级方案（USB/SD 卡导出日志） |
| 5 | 摄像头 sensor 驱动无现成支持 | 中 | 优先用 NuttX/ESP-IDF 已有支持的 sensor 型号，或先用官方 demo 库抓图 |
| 6 | 比赛分支代码变动 | 低 | 定期 `repo sync`，关注 `dev-ai-contest-2026` 分支更新 |
| 7 | 数据准备与标注耗时 | 中 | 提前开始采集 12 类手势数据；用数据增强扩大样本 |
## 八、待确认事项清单（评审会前请逐项确认）
1. 比赛是否提供 ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board 的 OpenVela BSP / 固件？在哪个分支？
2. PDF 硬件资料中板载摄像头 sensor 型号、屏幕分辨率/接口、音频 codec 型号、C6 与 P4 连接方式？（可把 PDF 关键页转成文字/图片发我，我帮你梳理驱动需求）
3. 比赛对“云端日志”有无指定平台？是否允许自建本地服务演示？
4. 手语手势定义：12 类具体是哪些字母/数字？有无标准数据集或必须自采？
5. 答辩/评分侧重（BSP 移植深度 vs 应用完整度 vs AI 效果），决定时间分配。
## 九、工具链与 VS Code 问题解答
**需要 VS Code 参与吗？——建议使用，但不是硬性必须。**
- OpenVela 官方提供 **VS Code 插件**（`vela.vs-aiot-ide-vela` + `vela.vela-preview`），支持图形化“创建项目 → 配置 defconfig → 编译 → 模拟器运行 → 断点调试”全流程，还带图片/字体/资源预览，**调试功能必须依赖该插件（C++ 插件）**，对学生很友好。
- 不装插件也能开发：命令行 `./build.sh <defconfig路径> -j$(nproc)` 编译 + esptool 烧录 + GDB 调试。
- **硬性前提**：VS Code 与插件必须在 **Ubuntu 22.04** 上运行（Windows 版 VS Code 无法编译 OpenVela，官方不支持 WSL/Docker）。
- 结论：**在 Ubuntu 22.04 上安装 VS Code + openvela 插件**，作为主力开发 IDE；命令行作为备用。
## 十、下一步建议动作（确认计划后执行）
1. 确认第八节“待确认事项”，尤其是比赛是否提供 P4 BSP；
2. 搭建 Ubuntu 22.04 环境 + VS Code + openvela 插件，跑通官方快速入门（模拟器）；
3. 开始 Phase 1 BSP 移植调研（先核对 OpenVela nuttx 是否有 esp32p4，无则评估上游代码量）；
4. 并行启动数据集收集与模型训练（Phase 6 前置）。

①项目名称与一句话定位：项目名称：面向听障群体的端侧静态手语手势翻译终端；面向听障人士简易日常沟通场景，基于ESP32‑P4‑Function‑EV‑Board开发板，摄像头采集静态手语手势，端侧AI识别，屏幕显示文字、播放语音播报，解决简单手语手势转可读语音文字的沟通障碍。
②目标开发板及选板理由：选用ESP32‑P4‑Function‑EV‑Board开发板；板载MIPI‑CSI 200万像素摄像头、7英寸电容触摸屏，内置NPU神经网络加速器、ISP图像处理单元，WiFi6蓝牙模组；原生支持OpenVela系统，硬件AI加速适合端侧图像推理，无需额外外接摄像头与显示屏，减少外设调试工作量，适合视觉AI类学生项目开发。
③核心功能：
1.摄像头采集手部图像，识别12种静态手语手势（字母、数字）；所需硬件能力：MIPI‑CSI摄像头、NPU、DMA。
2.板载屏幕实时渲染画面，显示识别翻译后的文字结果；所需硬件能力：MIPI‑DSI显示屏、LVGL图形。
3.识别成功后本地播放预合成语音播报翻译文本；所需硬件能力：I2S音频、扬声器。
4.Wi‑Fi上传识别记录，网页查看历史识别日志；所需硬件能力：WiFi6。
5.触摸屏幕切换识别模式、调整识别置信度阈值；所需硬件能力：电容触摸。
④各功能技术方案：
1.手语手势识别：端侧实现，PC端训练轻量化CNN模型，INT8量化；部署至OpenVela，调用板载NPU完成推理；摄像头图像经过ISP做裁剪灰度预处理，仅做静态手势图像分类，不做动态连续手语识别。
2.屏幕显示输出：端侧实现，OpenVela LVGL图形框架，渲染摄像头预览画面，输出识别结果文字到7寸触摸屏。
3.语音播报：端侧实现，存储预合成wav音频片段；识别匹配成功后直接播放对应音频，不使用端侧TTS，降低算力开销。
4.Wi‑Fi上传识别记录：端侧+云端，OpenVela网络组件HTTP协议上传JSON格式识别日志，浏览器访问网页查看历史记录。
5.触摸阈值配置：端侧实现，读取电容触摸输入，修改本地推理置信阈值参数。

## 你要做的是什么

**一个面向听障群体的端侧手语翻译终端**（比赛项目）：用 **ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board + OpenVela 系统**，摄像头拍下静态手语手势 → 端侧 AI 识别成文字 → 屏幕显示 + 语音播报。共 5 大功能：

1. 摄像头识别 **12 种静态手语手势**（字母/数字）
2. 板载 7 寸屏 LVGL 实时渲染 + 显示翻译文字
3. 识别后播放预合成 WAV 语音（不用端侧 TTS）
4. WiFi 上传识别记录，网页可查（有 USB/SD 降级预案）

I should answer honestly:

1. Feasibility: Yes, definitely achievable — and they've already done the hardest 30% (porting is nearly done). AI (like me, coding agents) can help with most of the code. But there are honest caveats about what AI can and can't do.

2. What AI API can help with (high leverage):
- Compile error debugging (they've already done 12 rounds with AI help)
- Writing drivers adaptation, defconfig, build fixes
- Model training pipeline (CNN + INT8 quantization with TensorFlow Lite)
- Data augmentation scripts
- LVGL UI code
- WAV audio generation (can even use TTS API to synthesize the 12 gesture words!)
- Web backend for logs (Flask)
- Documentation and 答辩 materials

3. Difficulties (honest assessment, ranked):
a. 真机调试 (hardware debugging) — this is the #1 difficulty that AI can't fully help with. Serial logs, oscilloscopes, wiring issues, driver bring-up on real hardware (MIPI-DSI LCD, MIPI-CSI camera, I2S audio, touch). AI can analyze logs but the physical iteration loop (flash → observe → debug) is slow and requires hands-on. This is where projects die.
b. 网络/环境问题 — GitHub access in China, mbedtls downloads, VPN issues (already hit)
c. Model accuracy on real hardware — INT8 quantization loss, camera image quality (lighting, background, skin color), 12-gesture dataset collection and labeling is laborious and quality matters
d. Real-time performance — TFLite Micro inference <300ms on RISC-V CPU
e. ESP32-C6 WiFi (SDIO/ESP-Hosted) integration maturity — they already have a downgrade plan
f. Integration complexity — 5 subsystems working together

4. Can it win? Honest assessment:
- Depends on the competition level (school? provincial? national? which competition?)
- For a student project: this is a fairly ambitious and complete project. BSP porting is a strong technical highlight (many teams avoid it)
- The project has a good social value angle (听障群体 social good)
- Realistic risks: hardware bring-up delays could eat the schedule; if board never lights up, demo fails
- Winning factors: working demo > slides; social value + technical depth combo
- Advice: secure the "board lights up + demo works" milestone early, and have a fallback (simulator demo + emulator)

Also address the "AI API" framing: clarify the difference between using AI as a coding assistant (what's been happening) vs. calling cloud AI APIs at runtime (cloud recognition). Important distinction! The competition likely requires 端侧 (on-device) processing — the plan explicitly says 端侧 AI 识别. So they can't just call a cloud API for the core recognition feature; they must run TFLite Micro on-device. However, AI APIs CAN be used during development (training assistance, code, audio synthesis, documentation) — and even as a data-collection tool (generate synthetic hand gesture images? Though real photos are better).

Actually, let me think about whether cloud API could do recognition as an alternative: The competition spec requires on-device edge AI (端侧), and the board has no guaranteed internet. Using cloud API for the core would violate the spirit and the 答辩 would be questioned. But could be a fallback for demo purposes. Better to keep TFLite Micro on-device as planned.

One more angle: they asked "我有一定的动手能力" — they're a student with moderate hands-on ability. The key question is whether this is realistic for them. Given they've already got porting to 80% compile stage, they're actually doing well. The realistic assessment: yes, achievable, but the hardware bring-up phase is the make-or-break point, and they should parallelize model training now.

Let me structure the answer:

## 二、AI 能帮你搞定什么（高杠杆清单）
1. 编译报错排错（已验证，12 处）
2. 驱动适配、defconfig、构建脚本
3. 模型训练全流程：数据集增强脚本、训练 CNN、INT8 量化、转 tflite、xxd 转 C 数组
4. LVGL 界面代码
5. 12 段语音：可以用 TTS API 生成（这个反而是"AI API 的合法用法"——预合成 WAV 本来就是方案里的）
6. 网页端日志服务（Flask）
7. 答辩材料、文档、PPT 大纲
8. 甚至数据采集辅助：生成手势图片做数据增强（注意：真实照片为主）

## 三、真正的难点（按风险排序，诚实版）
1. **真机调试（最大难点，AI 帮不了的部分）**——编译过了 ≠ 板子能跑。串口日志、MIPI-DSI 屏不亮、摄像头无图、I2S 无声、触摸没反应……这些是"烧录→观察→改→再烧"的物理循环，AI 只能帮你分析日志，不能替你插线、按复位键。项目挂掉 90% 挂在这里。
2. **数据集质量**——12 类手势要自己采集标注，数量和质量直接决定识别率。光照、背景、肤色、手型差异。没有现成标准数据集（公开的 ASL 数据集是字母，和中国比赛要求可能不一致）。
3. **INT8 量化精度损失**——PTQ 后准确率可能掉 5-10%，需要调校准集。
4. **性能预算**——400MHz 双核 RISC-V 跑 TFLite Micro，<300ms 延迟需要模型够小（<300KB），输入分辨率要压。
5. **时间管理**——BSP 移植已经吃掉大半时间；5 个功能 + 训练 + 文档，8-10 周很紧。
6. **网络环境**——GitHub 不稳定（已经踩过）。

block.text:
Good — OpenCode is the terminal AI coding agent (opencode.ai), officially supported by DeepSeek ([DeepSeek API docs: 接入 OpenCode](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/agent_integrations/opencode/)). So the user is comparing me (DeepSeek Harness agent in this GUI) vs OpenCode CLI agent, both running on DeepSeek API.

Now let me write the honest comparison. Key points:

1. Same "brain", different "body" — both run DeepSeek models; the difference is tooling, context, and where they operate.

2. Honest comparison table:
- Me (this agent): GUI at 3080, session context accumulated (I've read their full project), tools: file r/w, pwsh shell, glob/grep, web_search, subagents fan-out (workflow orchestration), background jobs, goal tracking. Running deepseek-v4-flash. Constrained: sandbox read-only currently, runs on Windows host, no direct access to the Ubuntu VM.
- OpenCode: terminal agent, runs directly in the repo directory (could be in the Ubuntu VM itself), Plan/Build modes, git integration, MCP, TUI. Officially supported by DeepSeek. Iteration loop in the actual source tree.

3. What actually determines success in THIS project:
- The bottleneck is NOT the agent — it's: (a) the Ubuntu VM where the 34GB source lives, (b) physical hardware bring-up, (c) network (GitHub).
- Compile-debug loop happens in the VM. Whoever can operate in the VM wins the loop.

4. My honest self-assessment:
- Where I'm stronger: accumulated project context (I know the plan/log/report), research + web search, parallel subagent fan-out, documentation/plans, long-run goal tracking, GUI for the user to review.
- Where OpenCode is stronger: if it runs inside the Ubuntu VM/terminal, it can edit the source tree directly and run the build loop hands-free; tighter feedback loop for pure coding tasks in a repo.
- Both same model family → code quality similar; difference is integration and workflow.

5. Practical recommendation: hybrid division of labor — e.g.:
- Me: 方案/调研/排错分析/文档/并行任务(数据集方案、训练脚本、答辩材料) 
- OpenCode (in the VM): 编译循环、源码修改、git 操作
- 真机调试: 只有你能做
- Or: me as "architect/orchestrator", OpenCode as "hands in the repo"; cross-review each other's changes.

6. Honest caveat: neither can flash/plug hardware; the human is the critical path. Also note which DeepSeek model they configured in each — model choice matters more than the wrapper (e.g., reasoner vs chat vs v4-flash). If they gave both the same model, the difference is pure tooling.

Also honest: I shouldn't oversell. The most honest statement: "完成得更好" 取决于把谁放在哪个环节 — 不是二选一，是配合。And the deeper truth: the critical path is the VM + hardware, not the AI.

Length: moderate. Use a table. Chinese. Cite the DeepSeek docs link for OpenCode.

说实话比——**这个问题的答案不是"谁更好"，而是"谁适合干哪一段"。** 你俩接的是同一个大脑（DeepSeek API），区别在"身体"（工具、运行环境、上下文），而且你这个项目的成败关键根本不在 AI 身上。我把话分三层说清楚。

---

## 一、先对齐事实：OpenCode 是什么

你指的应该是终端里的 AI 编程代理 **OpenCode（opencode.ai）**——DeepSeek 官方文档有专门的接入教程（[DeepSeek API 文档：接入 OpenCode](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/agent_integrations/opencode/)）。它和我一样是"读代码 → 改文件 → 跑命令 → 看结果"的自主循环代理。所以不是"两个 AI"，是**同一个模型、两套工具壳**。

## 二、诚实的对比

| 维度 | 我（这个 GUI 里的 agent） | OpenCode（终端代理） |
|------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| 项目上下文 | ✅ **我已读完全部项目文档**（计划书/日志/调研报告/目标），知道来龙去脉 | ❌ 每次新会话要重新喂上下文 |
| 并行能力 | ✅ 可以派多个子代理同时干活（比如同时调研驱动 + 起草训练方案） | ⚠️ 有子代理但偏单线 |
| 查资料 | ✅ 内置联网搜索，能查 HAL 接口、驱动型号、比赛规则 | ⚠️ 靠插件，弱一些 |
| 文档/方案 | ✅ 强项，适合写计划、答辩材料 | 一般 |
| 源码里死磕 | ⚠️ 我跑在 Windows 主机上，**碰不到你虚拟机里的 34GB 源码** | ✅ **如果你把 OpenCode 跑在 Ubuntu 虚拟机里，它能直接改源码、跑编译、看日志，闭环更快** |
| 编译排错 | ✅ 你喂日志给我，我分析给方案 | ✅ 它自己就能跑命令看日志 |
| 真机调试 | ❌ 碰不到硬件 | ❌ 同样碰不到 |

**结论一句话**：我强在"全局规划 + 并行调研 + 文档 + 有项目记忆"，OpenCode 强在"能直接钻进源码仓库里干活"。

## 三、你项目真正的关键（这比选谁都重要）

你的卡点从来不是"AI 不够强"：
1. **源码和编译环境在 Ubuntu 虚拟机里**——谁能操作那个环境，谁才能真正推进编译循环
2. **真机点亮只能你亲手做**——插线、烧录、看串口，AI 只能帮你分析日志
3. **网络**——GitHub 不稳，这个 AI 也解决不了

所以正确姿势不是二选一，是**分工**：

```
你（人）          → 真机调试、决策、网络问题
我               → 架构设计、编译报错分析、数据集/训练方案、
                   文档答辩材料、并行调研、帮你审 OpenCode 的改动
OpenCode（在虚拟机里）→ 源码级修改、编译循环、git 操作
```

还有个更实际的用法：**让 OpenCode 干活，把改动和报错日志发给我审**——两个 agent 互相 review，比单个 agent 盲干靠谱得多（它俩模型同源但上下文不同，能互相抓错）。

## 四、提醒你一个被忽略的变量

**你给两边配的是同一个模型吗？** DeepSeek API 有不同模型（chat / reasoner / v4-flash），模型选哪个对结果的影响**远大于**选哪个工具。如果两边都配一样的模型，那"谁更好"纯粹是工具层面的事；如果一边配了 reasoner 一边配了 flash，那先比模型再比工具。

---

**我的最终建议**：别押注单边。**OpenCode 负责虚拟机里"手"的活，我负责"脑"的活（方案、排错分析、文档、并行任务），你在中间做决策和真机调试**。要不要我现在先干一件具体的：把 `esp_gptimer.h` 那个卡点分析清楚，给你一份"直接丢给 OpenCode 或照着改"的修复方案？
